title: Quantum Chaos with a Macroscopic Zero-Mode Sector
authors: Cheryne Jonay, Kun W. Kim, Frank Pollmann, Alexander Altland
abstract: Chaotic many-body spectra are expected to densely fill their energy window. We show that constrained spin chains with chiral symmetry evade this expectation by hosting an exponentially large manifold of symmetry-protected exact zero modes separated from the surrounding spectrum by a sharp gap at zero energy. The gap is generated by chaotic level repulsion, with width set by the number of zero modes times the mean level spacing. We verify this mechanism in an East-West kinetically constrained chain, develop a minimal random-matrix description, and show how the gap can be detected through linear-response spectroscopy.
summary: The paper analyzes quantum spin chains exhibiting chiral symmetry to show that an exponentially large number of exact zero-energy states creates a distinct spectral gap. By combining random matrix theory with linear response spectroscopy, the authors demonstrate how this gap and the associated degeneracy can be robustly detected experimentally, distinguishing it from standard chaotic behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates how chiral symmetry protects an exponentially large manifold of exact zero modes in many-body quantum systems, fundamentally altering the surrounding energy spectrum.
main_result: These zero modes create a hard spectral gap at zero energy ($\Delta \sim \mu\delta$), which can be diagnosed using linear-response spectroscopy and spectral form factor analysis.
method: The authors employ chiral random matrix theory (chRMT) alongside linear response theory to analyze spectral correlations and the influence of symmetry on low-energy excitations.
model_or_system: The primary model is constrained spin chains, specifically the East–West (EW) model, which possesses chiral ($\Gamma$), translational ($T$), and inversion ($I$) symmetries. A Star-Graph model is also analyzed for comparison.
key_observables: Density of states near E=0 ($ho(E)$), spectral form factor $K(t)$, linear response susceptibility $\chi(\Omega)$, and the gap width $\Delta$.
important_parameters: The number of zero modes ($\mu$), the mean level spacing ($\delta$), and system size ($L$). The ratio $\Delta/\delta \sim \mu$ is a key scaling parameter.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that symmetries remain intact to preserve both degeneracy and gap; approximations are made in linear response theory by simplifying matrix element contributions.
figures_summary: Figures compare the spectral density of states ($ho(E)$) for different models (chGOE, EW, Star-graph), showing distinct lower edge shapes. Another figure illustrates how linear response susceptibility $\chi(\Omega)$ reveals a zero-mode resonance peak when symmetry is preserved.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the existence of zero modes via symmetries in the EW model, quantifying the resulting spectral gap using RMT and form factors, and finally probing this structure dynamically using linear response spectroscopy to distinguish between models based on edge shape and low-frequency response.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how topological or crystalline symmetries enforce macroscopic degeneracies in quantum spectra, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum simulators or studying exotic phases of matter.
